points.description: Initialisation: the neurons/weights are arranged in a lattice topology suited to the problem, and the weight vectors are initialised randomly (all different). Equivalent wording earns the mark.

Sampling and similarity matching: an input is drawn from the input space and matched to the most similar neuron, which becomes the winning neuron (e.g. by minimum Euclidean distance or an equivalent best-matching rule).
Weight update: the weights of the winning neuron and of its neighbours are updated, with the neighbours set by a neighbourhood function.

Decay and looping: the neighbourhood size and learning rate are reduced over time, and the process repeats (keep sampling) until ordering/convergence is reached, then stops. A loop or iteration structure in the pseudocode counts.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.25 if only one half is given: either the decay of the neighbourhood/learning rate, or the repeat-until-convergence loop.
